paragraphs: On Friday evening, Lily sat at the kitchen table with a poster. Tom came in and looked at it. "What are you going to do tomorrow?" asked Tom. "Mia and I are going to a space exhibition," said Lily. "It is in the town hall, and it opens at ten o'clock." "Space?" said Tom. "I love space. Is there a spaceship?" "Yes, there is a big model spaceship," said Lily. "You can go inside." "Then I will come, too," said Tom.

"Wait," said Lily. "I must read the details first." She read the poster slowly. "It opens at ten and closes at four," she said. "The price is twenty baht, and tickets are available at the door." "But there are only two hundred tickets for each day." "Only two hundred?" said Tom. "Then we must go early."

"I will ask Dad to take us at half past nine," said Lily. "Good idea," said Tom. "Dad will drive, because the bus is slow on Saturday." "Is the exhibition on the ground floor?" he asked. Lily looked at the poster again. "No, it is on the second floor," she said. "We will take the stairs." "Then I am going to run up," said Tom. "You will be tired before you see the spaceship," said Lily with a laugh.

Dad came into the kitchen and sat down. "What are you two planning?" he asked. "We are going to the space exhibition tomorrow," said Tom. "Will you drive us there?" "Of course," said Dad. "I will be ready at half past nine." "What will you see there?" he asked. "There is a model of every planet," said Lily. "And there is a puzzle table for children."

"Mia is going to try the puzzle," said Lily. "I am going to look at the spaceship," said Tom. "What time will you come home?" asked Dad. "At one o'clock," said Lily. "We will call you from the town hall." Pip sat under the table and looked at them. "Pip, you cannot come," said Lily. "A spaceship is not a place for dogs." "He will wait at home," said Dad with a smile.
